description: QA Test Plan v3 — BatchExporter (Blender 4.0+ Extension)
notes: Contains only tests that failed or had concerns in v2. 20 passed tests removed. Fixes applied: scene switching for cross-scene export, drive validation for invalid paths, ensure_output_dir moved inside try/except.

categories.title: Bug Fix Re-verification
categories.description: Tests that failed in v2 and were fixed. Must be re-run to confirm the fixes.

tests.title: Export by Scenes — Cross-Scene Fix
tests.origin: v2 test 1.1 (FAILED — only current scene exported)
tests.bug_fixed: _gather_by_scene() was filtering by current view layer, excluding objects from other scenes. Fixed by removing the view layer filter and adding scene switching in _export_items() so each scene's objects are reachable.
steps: Create 2 scenes, each with at least 1 mesh object
Open Batch Export, set scope to 'Scenes'
Set output dir, format to FBX, click OK
expected: One .fbx file per scene, named after the scene
Both scenes are exported (not just the active one)
Each file contains the meshes from that scene
Info area shows correct succeeded count (2)
After export, the active scene is restored to Scene 1

tests.title: Export All Objects — Cross-Scene Fix
tests.origin: v2 test 1.2 (FAILED — objects in other scenes not exported)
tests.bug_fixed: _gather_all() was iterating only bpy.context.view_layer.objects. Fixed to iterate all scenes with deduplication, and _export_items() now switches scene before exporting each item.
steps: Create 2 scenes: Scene 1 with 3 mesh objects, Scene 2 with 2 mesh objects
Open Batch Export, set scope to 'All Objects'
Set output dir, format to FBX, click OK
expected: Five individual .fbx files created (one per mesh across both scenes)
No duplicate files for objects that appear in multiple scenes
After export, the active scene is restored to Scene 1

tests.title: Invalid Output Path — Clean Error
tests.origin: v2 test 1.4 (FAILED — full traceback chain printed to console)
tests.bug_fixed: Two fixes: (1) ensure_output_dir() now validates the drive/root anchor exists before attempting mkdir, giving a clean error. Uses 'from None' to suppress chained tracebacks. (2) ensure_output_dir() call moved inside try/except in _export_items() so the error is caught and recorded in the report.
steps: Set output directory to a non-existent drive (e.g. 'Z:\nonexistent\path')
Select an object and attempt to export
expected: Export fails gracefully with a single clean error line
Error message includes 'drive or root' and 'does not exist'
No chained traceback (no 'During handling of the above exception' spam)
Report shows 0 succeeded, 1 failed with error details

tests.title: Export at Origin — No Unwanted Directory Creation
tests.origin: v2 test 4.4 (PASSED with concern — 'instead of failing, the program created the directory, this is dangerous')
tests.bug_fixed: ensure_output_dir() now validates the drive/root anchor exists before calling mkdir(parents=True). Paths on non-existent drives are rejected immediately. Creating subdirectories on valid drives remains intentional behaviour.
steps: Set output to a path on a non-existent drive (e.g. 'Z:\some\deep\path')
expected: Export fails with a clean error about the drive not existing
No directories are created on the non-existent drive
The object's location is restored to (5, 10, 3) even after failure
On a valid drive, subdirectories ARE created as expected (this is normal behaviour)
